title: Josh Johnson Arizona Cardinals Press Conference 11.22.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: you've been through situations like this before and how you got through this one with this team kind of how are you feeling right now? >> Um obviously very disappointed. Um just you know I understand you know the the magnitude of the situation playing against a a great team like Kansas City and just really just reflecting back on the game immediately without looking at the film. you know, like we had we had moments that we needed to capitalize on as a offense to really just keep the game where it needed to be and uh you know, so I'm gonna look at myself first, you know, the things that I could have did differently better and just grow from there and then uh you know, get back to work. >> You said Friday that you were going to be realistic about the situation. >> You've only got one day of reps. >> Yeah. Did it go as you expected in terms of how running? [snorts] >> Um, no. I mean, I felt like we had opportunity to score like, you know, we were moving the ball, but you you know, you get across the 50, you know, we we we all out. Uh, you know, I took that sack one time. Can't do that. We had penalties. Um, and you know, uh, like the third down on the two minute, you know, I was really just frustrated in how I read that play out. Uh, and you know, those are the things that come in this in these moments. But, you know, I'm not I'm not the person that's going to like make an excuse about that. Like, my job was my job is to go out there and help this team win. And I didn't do my job today cuz we [snorts] we wasn't in a position to win. So, I mean, we all as a team, we probably all felt like that as players. At least we should, you know. So, it's not it's not something right now that, you know, you necessarily feel good about. You know, I'm grateful for the opportunity. You know, I feel like we made some plays here and there. We show him flashes, but flashes versus good teams don't get you nothing. >> Trey, we all know that he's going to get attention. I mean, obviously, you targeted him a number of times. How do you feel like that connection? >> Um, it was okay. Um there was a couple that I that you know as with more time on task with him that I'll let him do his thing a little bit more. Um I didn't want to try to overthink things because of the what was of just understanding that there's so much things that I don't understand like in regards to how guys react in games. And so like you know just going back over and I told him on the field you know like you know there was things that I you know I owe you in regards to just this opportunities just to keep us on task especially when they're going to double him and then when you get the chances to get him oneonone you just got to make those count. >> Even though you been around for a while having one day of rep can you put put in perspective how hard is that to take that >> um it's it's challenging you know what I mean? I think it's not just challenging on myself, it's challenging on the guys. Like how do how I talk, how I communicate, you know, all those things is new and we're we're figuring that out in the moment. You just can't really dwell on that because that's that's that's just what it is. That's something you can't control, you know. Um but yeah, it's challenging, you know, just I think, you know, with a week of practice and things like that, you able to really kind of go through everything the best way and physically get those reps, but like I honestly not wasn't worried about that, man. And I was worried about trying to score points for the Arizona Cardinals and just do what I can and and I and as of right now that's kind of what I'm focused on like how how can I help whether that be if I'm out here or whether I'm not out here like what can I do to help improve this situation >> with uh Carson's back being what it is and coach was saying basically there spasms we got and see how it goes. Obviously that puts everybody in kind of an awkward situation including yourself. I'm sure it's going to be you and it's not going to be like how do you handle that or with everything you've been through in your career, does that not really impact you? >> It don't impact me honestly. It's it's what it is. Uh it's my job to uh really focus on how I can get myself to a comfort level to go out there and execute and that's kind of what really all I focus on honestly. >> You get those reps starting Wednesday. How much growth can you get in a week with guys in terms of getting on the same page and >> Yeah. Oh no, for sure. There's a lot of growth and it just it's also the nuances, you know, like if they do this, we could do that. You know what I mean? Like how I'm thinking like this, like you we you don't get those conversations at the one day. You kind of sprinkle that in throughout the game, you know, um watching film if something show up, but like really kind of diving through it, understanding how each guy is thinking about these plays. We didn't get that this week, you know, and it it's what it is, you know. Thanks, Josh. >> All right. Thank you, guys.

title: Caleb Williams on performance vs. Saints | Press Conference
text: Uh, got it. Got it. You're all good, man? Good? Okay. Just checking in on you. >> Caleb, coming off of a bye week, how would you assess the offense's performance this week? >> Yeah. Um, I think we can be a lot better. Um, I think there was opportunity for a lot of points out there. Um, whether it's just us being on the same page, whether it's um, you know, us us being efficient running and and efficient passing. And so um, yeah, I think there's there was a lot more uh, that we left out there um, and that we can be better at this next week coming up. >> Seems like the last two games the mood in the locker room and mood in here has been not necessarily one of people were satisfied. >> Yep. Uh, no. Um, putting up uh, how many points we put up today uh, with how the defense played. I know we put up 13 points off of turnovers. And so being able to uh, have that is great. Um, but but no. Not not uh, not satisfied. >> What did you see on on the leveling dribble? >> Uh, I got a great view of it. Um, it was pretty cool to be able to uh, see him uh, go up and and make a play for the team. >> You passed to Zay what did you see on that play? >> Which one? >> The 40 yarder down the uh, >> Left sideline? Um, yeah. Um, they took away uh, the first read. Um, and then from there uh, Zay ran a great route. Uh, got inside, uh, broke it over the top. And uh, he flashed and uh, just gave him a good ball. >> Slight went on the backside? >> Yeah, he made a he made a hell of a catch right there. Uh, couldn't get all of it uh, all all of it uh, behind the throw uh, because of uh, I think it was Studsman uh, right there uh, right next to me running with me. And so uh, he made a made a aggressive movement. Uh, we you know, we locked eyes. And uh, he came back and made a play for us. >> What did the 40 yarder do for momentum there? You guys had just taken the sack. We're third and long. And it felt like it felt like you you guys were able to get >> Yeah. Um, yeah, when you have when you have those uh, super explosives, what we call them, they always a good bit of momentum. And so, uh, I said, he ran a great route. Just gave him a shot. O-line did a great job. And so, um, yeah. >> What what have you learned about your team throughout this winning streak? The way you guys go about your business each week and each game? >> Yeah, we we win in multiple ways and and that's good for us as a as a team to know that when we get in these situations throughout the year and and late in this, you know, late in this year, you know, we got each other's back and and we know that you know, we can win in in a multitude of ways. >> The fact that you guys haven't trailed since you came back. >> Yeah. >> How do you balance that with the fact that it it kind of feels like there's some meat left off the bone offensively? >> Yeah, more. That's it. >> Taylor, what what's your thoughts on Dylan Chase Young and Granderson today? They got to you a couple times, but you alluded that most of the time. What are your thoughts on their their ability to put pressure on a quarterback? >> Yeah, I think coming into this game, I think they had 16 plus sacks together, 16 and 1/2 or so. Um, and so they've been having a hell of a year. And so, just just trying not to let them, you know, get going. You never want to allow the defensive line to build confidence. And so, you know, they they did a great job. They got me a few times. And other than that, I was trying to just make a play for the team. And so, yeah, find ways to get better and not have those those sacks. >> From your vantage point, what kind of juice does Jeffrey Simmons bring for you guys when he's making plays out there and bringing that energy? >> Yeah, he he's a he's a momentum changer. Swings the momentum in our favor a lot of times. And so, having him on the team, having him making plays for us, having him bringing the energy, having him lead is is is been awesome. It's been fun. It's been able to It's been fun to be able to to watch myself. >> Quick turnaround before Thursday. >> Yep. >> What's your interpretation of the stakes of that game given that it's within the division and against a team that you guys haven't beaten in the last >> Yeah, it's it's it's an division game. So obviously it matters a lot for us as as a record and as as division cuz we we haven't won you know, that we're we're 0 and 2 and and of it. And so it's it's a big game for us. We got to go out there. We got to execute. We got to do all the things that that good teams do. We got to get up tomorrow. We got to prepare. We got to rest our bodies. We got to do like I said, all the things that that good teams do and winning teams do. And you know, that's a that's a obviously a worthy opponent over there. >> What do you and the offense need to do to get where you want to be by Thursday? >> Yeah, just talk, communicate, figure out what we did wrong in this game and whether it's energy, momentum, whether it's you know, building plays off of each other, successful plays off of each other, just just go back and look at the film. >> All set. Thank you. >> Awesome.

title: Panthers Live Press Conference
text: [music] >> Oh. >> [music] >> Thank you. >> Yeah. >> Hey, how about the fight in this group, you know, to just continue to battle all the way through it and uh some moments that we missed, some opportunities missed um and Baltimore taking advantage, having a heck of a drive going down there, finding a touchdown to take the lead, but the guys just sticking together, uh finishing those those couple of drives, getting the field goal to go ahead, and then of course the big interception. Um speaks to the character of the group, something that we know about these guys. What's out there for us? We got to take advantage of the moments in this game where we had an opportunity to really create some distance. Um some red zone opportunities down there offensively speaking and uh just capitalizing on the turnovers that the defense was creating out there. That's something that collectively we have to be able to cash in on. Um that has to play into our favor. >> The play between the fourth fumble that Will had at the goal line, that tipped ball, I mean, where does this kind of rank in the pantheon of rookie performances? >> Uh I think that the effort, um the willpower on that long run that was going to be a touchdown and for Will to punch it out um is going to go down as one of my favorite plays since I've been the coach here and it'll be something that we'll point to. This is how we play football, that you you never give up. As long as you got a blade of grass and it's not across the goal line, everything you got cuz you just never pass judgment on what's going to happen. An unbelievable play there. Um and then to get the other punch out and then at the end, you know, the going up for an interception, tipping it and T. Dot ends up with the interception. What an amazing comeback for Will Lee uh after spending some time off to uh show up for his guys that way. >> Obviously still some penalties today, probably you want back, but significantly less than the past few weeks. Uh what was different in the conversation this week with maybe in the locker room? >> Just being more conscientious of the pre-snap stuff. Um that was a lot cleaner. And then of course after the play, um I think we had a couple of uh unnecessary roughness penalties, but you know, the things [clears throat] that I was looking for the guys to clean up was let's celebrate together with us. Um let's make sure that we don't divert any energy to the opponent. Bring it back to our sideline. Get guys going. And the guys responded well that way. >> How was Coker? >> Uh he was they're still going to evaluate him. So tomorrow will be uh the continual evaluation there. Um so got really nothing after that. >> Was that a concussion protocol >> Yes. Yes. >> Dave, suddenly lead changes is the second most in the league this year. For you guys to constantly be able to fight back as an offense, what did you see from that group and from Brad in his play calling? >> The I mean the balance was there. Um the run game got going. You know, we started to hit some passes. We evened out the explosives in the second half. You know, we started off um it was really about tackling for our defense um in the first half and we settled in. They still made a couple of plays. Uh Derek Henry's nice long run there. We got to get him down in those situations and so uh that's something that we can talk about and and clean up from a technical standpoint. But the offense had balance in moving the ball, but we got to finish with touchdowns in the red zone when we get those opportunities. >> Um you you end up now after all the results today, two games clear in the NFC South. Um obviously you're following that. What what does that say about this team and where you are right now? >> It was a challenge that I posed to the team and I don't really like to talk about anything other than our game. Um but it was a moment to recognize and I wanted the guys to be comfortable in this position to be able to say, hey, when you have a chance to start to create some distance, how do we respond to that? And uh just to create that, you know, a little added pressure and I never really want to make it about the bigger story, but the goal is to win the division. And when you have a moment like this, um it's important to be able to play our best ball in these moments. >> Dave, an kind of an up and down day for the defense but the ability to slam the door at the end. What did you like about the the finish from them? >> Yeah. Uh I mean really it was every time they took the grass and the energy was right. The guys were talking together, working through things, sticking together, excited to get back out and get another opportunity and um really get him into the halftime and uh just talking to each other, guys, we got to show up and we got to get these guys down. Let's give the Baltimore Ravens a lot of credit. Um Jacoby Brissett settling in with that group of skill players. I you know, um I could see that happening. I was really hoping it it wasn't going to be today. Um and uh Jacoby did an excellent job distributing. Uh Zay Flowers got going. You know, obviously the run got going and uh everyone could see what what a good one-two punch they have with Derek Henry and with Justice Hill to be able to make some big plays. So we settled in and the guys stuck together and and finished on the right terms. >> You spent a lot of one-on-one time with Princely Umanmielen. The performance that he had today, just getting to the quarterback but also just affecting the pass in general, how much has he grown this year? >> Yeah, I mean the important part for Princely is he's a very passionate and emotional guy and the important part is in the flow of it, when a play goes your way or doesn't, go to the next play and just keep your focus on the possibilities of what could happen on the very next play and that's what I saw for him. I saw a very a very clear-headed young player looking for his opportunities to go out there and help his team all the way to the end getting that nice sack on that stunt. >> Trick play from when Coker took the snap. How long has that been in your back pocket? How did that come about? >> It's it's been about I want to say it's 3 weeks, but for sure the last 2 weeks just kind of working through the timing of it all and you know, the biggest part is obviously Coker getting the ball to Bryce and making sure that exchange is right. That's the most critical part of the play and and then I was just you know, so glad to see especially because they got us on a on a beautiful wildcat double pass for a touchdown earlier in the game and it was great to just be able to flip that part of it and and get one of our own. >> The challenge on the on the second Will Levis forced fumble, was that something you saw or were you notified about that? >> Well, I saw it live, but I really wasn't sure and and George Lee's upstairs in the box and he was like he caught it on the first step and there's two more right after it and and our you know, stadium game day ops did a phenomenal job of giving us a look up there so we can be even more confident, you know, cuz they weren't looking at it. So they forced me to challenge it, but I had a lot of help on that and and I wanted to give us an opportunity there. >> We saw Bryce react after he picked up the personal foul when Hendrickson landed on him. What did you see in that play? What did you think of how he and I think also Rasheed reacted? >> My eyes were kind of down on the coverage, so I didn't really see what happened till I looked back and saw the flag um on the ground, but you know, the guys are the guys are in the moment competitive and you know, that's kind of you get to get a sneak peek into Bryce's mentality and while he looks cool, calm and collected most of the time, you know, there's this passionate burning competitor inside that uh that sometimes he lets all of us see, so. >> You know you were looking for more production from the receivers from after last week. What did you think of T-Mac and Coker's game, but also the tough catches they made in >> Yeah, I mean they did a good job covering us and being available. It there were some tight windows. Bryce found them and the guys made some incredible catches in traffic, getting hit, uh finishing those plays and I was fired up to see that and again that's a tribute to the whole group working through that together. It's Bryce, um it's the boys, it's Brad, you know, just finding different ways to find voids for our guys. >> Duce Vaughn had three opportunities to make a big play on special teams. What did you say to him on the sideline hacking him back up? >> Uh lots of teachable moments, you know, making making sure don't get cute. Um you know, when you when you have a ball that's down at the three, we don't need it at the six inch line. If it's inside the five, that's good enough, so we'll be able to coach off of that. Um just maintaining your composure on that that muff punt, you know, and being able to secure the ball first. You want to scoop and score right there. At a minimum, let's get the ball. Let's end up with it and so um a couple of teachable moments right there. >> Dave, what do you think of going back to Bryce for a second? What do you think of how he orchestrated that final drive? Um I believe two completions on third third and six, third and seven. >> Game on the lines. Nobody else I want with the ball. Bryce Young's going to go there. He's going to be he's going to be in control. He's going to be focused and locked into the moment and that's what he looked like on that drive. >> But what about his play in the first half, first few quarters? >> Yeah, we're moving the ball. Um he was finding explosives. He was finding completions off of his first and second progression, so I loved that, loved the rhythm that he was in and he'd be the first one up here to tell you he'd love to have a couple of red zone opportunities back to really take this offense to the next step and that's something that we've been talking about working on and uh a challenge that the guys will accept. >> Dave, it feels like >> found on >> your challenge to the team and when did that happen? >> What's that? >> Can you expound on your challenge to the team and when did that happen? >> was early in the week and just kind of identifying the moment where you get these these moments during the season, whether it's in the middle of the season or late where you have a chance and you're in the you're in the driver's seat and we have to be comfortable with these situations and be able to play our best football and that was a good game. I'm glad we finished. There's another level. There's another layer for us to have that killer instinct to be able to put the foot on the gas and and run away with games. >> Hey, you had a big game ball guy. Were you tempted to give Will one tonight? >> I really was. You know, Will you know, had a phenomenal game, especially his first time going back out there and if I was to give a game ball out, I would definitely have given it to Will Levis. >> Hey, you ran Trevor in the throw bit. How how hard is it to kind of balance in your mind getting Chuba a break versus the way he's running the ball right now? >> Yeah, I mean the volume that Chuba's getting I'm just kind of watching it live to see what he looks like as he runs so hard in that style and and it's good to have fresh legs to come in there and you know, Trevor from the moment he came back and he was available his when we were available to get him back, he showed us from the first time he stepped out on the practice field that he meant business. He wants to help this team and you know, when he when he carried the ball, he was sprinting through the defense and going to the goal line when he was returning it in special teams periods during practice. He's just screaming all over the field, really just talking to us with his body language about wanting to help this team and each time he gets an opportunity in offense, he just keeps getting better and better. That's the type of mentality we're looking for guys. Tell me that you want us to get you out there and and Trevor is really doing some good things in on offense and in the special teams game. >> Thank you, coach. >> All right, thank you. >> kind of as a unit and how you've just grown to rely on them. >> Yeah. They work so hard. They did such a great job today running the pass game. They did a I wish everyone got to see what they get to do throughout the week. Just the way they attack the meetings, the way they attack practices, the the attention to detail they have. So it's it's great for for for them and for us obviously when we're able to lean on them like we did all game. It all starts with that. So yeah, I'm super grateful for that unit. >> Your first touchdown to Mitch Evans came on that trick play. Can you just kind of walk us through how that developed and what it's like for you not taking the snap and into the >> Yeah. Lowkey I think that was like my first time ever doing that. So it was fun. But yeah, all the credit goes to to Brad and all the guys upstairs for the creativity, drawing something up like that. And Mitch doing a great job having Phil um, you know, catching transition and falling into the end zone. Um, so uh, yeah, it was fun doing doing something, you know, a little different like that. Um, and then obviously able to end it with a touchdown is always great. So uh, yeah, great execution from from the guys. >> Bryce Bryce, paraphrasing Dave, he just said with the game on the line, there's no one you'd rather have the ball in his hands than you. Given all you guys have been through over the last three years, the ups and downs, like what does that mean to you to hear something like that and have that trust? >> Yeah, no, it means a lot. Um, you know, obviously everything that uh, I want to do, us as a unit, we want to go out do uh, go out and do is is uh, to have his back and protect him out on the field. Um, so we talk about it all the time, you know, when we're out there, whoever's carrying the ball, you carry the hopes and dreams of of the organization, everything like that. So um, in those moments um, I trust the guys around me. Um, we all kind of rally off of each other. Um, so again, I'm super proud of the guys finding a way down there um, to to get three. And then our defense, um, you know, finishing it on our terms, them getting a turnover um, in a game like that, it's huge. So it's a it's a team effort. Um, but yeah, Nudge definitely uh, definitely means a lot. >> Bryce, so on that final drive >> I was from your vantage point, how did you experience Will Levis' performance today? >> Yeah, uh, I mean, talk about making big plays. Um, you know, those were huge game shifting uh, you know, turnovers you were able to cause. Um, you know, the energy that he plays with, you know, we feel it throughout the week and obviously it translates to Sundays. Um, but yeah, especially for for for a young guy having such heads up plays like he did, um, it's it's super impressive. So he he works super hard. I'm excited to to watch him continue to keep growing. >> Bryce, on that final drive, um, that connection with T-Mac, I think it was third and six, can you take us through that play? It looked like um, you went through like three or four uh, options before you landed on T-Mac. >> Yeah, um, that's just a great job of T-Mac winning. Um, especially versus a really cloudy look, honestly. Sent two guys over there at him, still found a way to win and um, progressed back to him I I always trust him. Um in situations like that, of course, um really really anytime. Uh you know, that's the type of player he is. So for him to win, um you know, go up and and make a catch like that over the middle, um no fear, um that's the type of player competitor he is. >> Bryce, how would you describe your interaction with Trey Hendrickson on that play where you coming off? >> Uh we were just just just chopping up a little bit. Um you know, nothing nothing malicious or anything like that. I have a lot of respect for for him for them as a team and as a defense. Um you know, yeah, it wasn't just just a little uh you know, in game back and forth. Nothing nothing bad. >> Bryce, I know you we rarely see you we we rarely see you fired like that. What what spawned what spawned that just getting hit hit as hard as you did by Trey? >> Um really just just wanting to help the team. It's not a emotional thing. It's just wanting to um you know, I guess uh you know, do whatever we can to to get a 15 that moves the moves the uh the drive. Um so yeah, it's not emotional. The refs, all that stuff, um yeah, they have a tough job. It's it's not ever uh you know, trying to throw them under the bus or anything like that. Uh just again, whatever it takes to move the team as as the cue that that's my job. >> Bryce, uh the bulk of the homegrown guys on this team or on this offense are on pace to have career years. Well, from your perspective, what has Brad brought to this offense that has allowed you guys to do all all that you guys do? >> Yeah, um I mean a a a a lot of things. Um you know, first off, I think just the um the belief um and the confidence that not just on Sundays, but he instills throughout the week in all of us. Um I feel like he he he does a great job of um you know, having us take ownership, you know, being you know, there are a lot of guys you can go out and you know, if you're a play caller, you can go and be hardheaded and not want to listen to anyone. And and this staff and and Brad for sure, um they want to have our input. They want to have conversations. They want us to have a dialogue. Um and I think that empowers all of us to want to go out there, perform, have his back. Um and of course, the the the creativity and stuff we do, um you know, the the play timing, um he does a great job has a great feel with all that stuff. So, um, we're super grateful for him. And, you know, as an offense, we we want to make sure that we we have his back um, the same way that he has ours uh throughout the weekend Sundays. >> Dave said he challenged you guys early in the week to, you know, create some distance in this division race. Besides winning obviously, how did you guys how did you feel your teammates and yourself kind of understood that challenge and responded? >> Yeah. Um, really just want to go 1 and 0. Um, you know, uh I think for us it's you have to be where your feet are. Obviously, there's stuff at stake um, and you know, there's stuff around, but uh in this league, you know, you can't look left or right. You got to look right ahead of you. Um, and you know, I'm I'm super proud of how the team did that this week. We found a way. Um, we'll celebrate it for, you know, these 24 and then we have to do the same thing. We have to flush it regardless of what happens. Um, we just want to go 1 and 0 next week. So, um, for us I think that's that's the mindset. >> Speaking of celebration, other than watching tape, any Thanksgiving plans? Anything >> Uh, I got to see what they they have us doing. Um, yeah, it'll yeah, whatever they they tell me that'll that'll affect that. >> That interception in the in the red zone, can you kind of take us through what you saw and then um, how were you able to kind of flush it and bounce back? >> Yeah, yeah. Um, want to make a play and obviously can't turn the ball over um, in that scenario in that part of the field. Um, take full accountability for that. Um, [snorts] uh one you you know, I definitely want back. Um, but you got to flush it. Um, again it's it is what it is. Uh, you can't let one play be more than just that. Um, go out there again I I rally around my guys. Um, you know, I draw my confidence from from Christ. I I know whatever it is you you turn the page and again I'm super grateful for the fight um, of this team, for the resilience and uh ups or downs there's no you know, I I don't want to be out there with. So, that that part's easy. >> Thank you, guys. >> Hello

title: Christian Watson: 'We know what's at stake' in matchup vs. the Rams
text: What was your first time? You have the same number of days off either way, I guess, but do you miss having it all week or is it whatever ? Uh yeah, no, I mean, it's definitely not that, you know, useful, when you don't have it, you know, in one big block.  I mean, splitting it up, you know, isn't necessarily the same as simply having, you know, a week off. Uh, but I mean, it is what it is.  Well, you know, you have to accept it and move on .  But I mean, obviously we still have to take advantage of both breaks and, you know, give the body, give the mind , you know, a little reset. So, what was your first reaction when the schedule came out and the word Wednesday was there for a game? Uh, I mean, obviously it was, you know, definitely a little bit different. Um, but like I said, at the end of the day, you know, that's out of our control.  Uh, you just have to accept, you know, the challenges along the way and, um, you know, obviously it's a good opportunity too to, you know, have, you know, that first Thanksgiving Eve game.  Uh, you know, obviously it's a prime- time opportunity for us.  So, we just have to accept the challenge and look forward to it. What's the challenge with that high school? They obviously brought in a couple of cornerbacks during the offseason. Yeah, no, I mean, they 're definitely a solid group.  Um, you know, I think , you know, the biggest challenge is, you know, combining that, you know, with the front line they have. Uh, you know, having a solid high school , you know, and obviously, you know, having the guys they have up front makes it a challenge in every way.  But, you know, at the end of the day, we do what we have to do. Uh, you know, we'll still be able to make plays, we'll still be able to do what we need to do.  So, let's see how it goes. What's the feeling or what's the energy like here? Because obviously, the team talks a lot about trying to go 1-0, but you know what's at stake in games like these where, you know, it matters more.   You know, what's it like? Do you feel that urgency or is everything still business as usual? Uh, I mean, a little bit of both.  I mean, we definitely feel the urgency.  Uh , I mean, I think, you know, even at the beginning of the year, just, you know , having, um, you know, obviously early NFC North games and all that.  I mean, every game is equally important to me, you know, as a player.  But, uh, I mean, we're definitely feeling the urgency, but, you know, obviously we can't , you know, overdo it and, you know, try to go out there and try to do too much or anything.  I mean, we just have to do our job and, you know, let everything else work itself out, but, I mean, at the end of the day, the urgency is definitely there.  We know what's at stake.  Uh, you know, we know the opportunity we have in front of us, so I just have to take advantage of it.   Do you think something like that makes you play better or worse? Um, I mean, it depends on how you accept it, you know, how you deal with it , but, I mean, I think at the end of the day, we're all high-level competitors, so, at the end of the day it should make you play better .  Um, I mean, you know, the moments of high competitiveness and high risk, um, is, you know, where the real competitors shine, so , um, it should make us play better. Christian, what kind of boost does Mike give you when he comes back? Wow, huge.  I mean, he's one of the best players in the National Football League, so, uh, having him back there, uh, you know, just his presence there will be something important for us. Uh, you know, obviously just the energy he'll bring, uh, just with his style of play and just, you know, even his energy on the sidelines will be huge, so definitely excited, uh, that he's back there. Christian, regarding the offense and with Caleb, based on what he's done in the ground attack these last few weeks, what kind of spark is he giving you guys to get the ground game going and help you out a bit? Um, I mean, it's important to see, you know, obviously the ability that our runners have. You know, obviously we have to keep improving, you know, around them, better forwards to give them more opportunities and just keep pushing everyone to move this forward even further, because I think we all agree that we're not where we want to be yet in terms of the ground game, so it's great to see.   We just need to keep improving around it .  Uh, you know, I think it's just as important for us receivers at the second level to get those blocks, to be able to turn those three- or four- yard runs into ten- or fifteen- yard runs. Uh, so you know, it's something very important.  We just have to keep going, you know, keep moving forward.

title: Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes, George Karlaftis & Emmett Johnson Postgame Press Conferences-NFL Week 11
text: First of all, congratulations to the KC Current for the big win yesterday. What a great job they did. Um. And then uh to our fans, we appreciate the support every week that we have a chance to play at home. They bring great energy, help our players with the energy part of it. Do a tremendous job. As far as the injuries go, Noah Gray got hit in the ribs. We'll just see how he he does. And then uh on Summerlin tweaked his knee there. So other than that, we we came out pretty healthy. A lot of a lot of good individual things that that took place, but most of all the the defense and the offense and special teams all were productive. So as you go through the names, there's people from all areas there that contributed in a big way. Defensively with Tranquill, you ended up having eight tackles, George two and a half sacks. Noel, who's playing real good football right now, our corner, young guy. Love seeing these young guys stepping up and and making plays like they're doing right now. They're growing right before our eyes and that's important as you work through this part of your of your season. Pat had a big day on the offensive side. Kelce, Emmit, another young kid that's just playing his tail off here. Got over 100 yards. Downs, Rice, Worthy had a touchdown, right, which was a joke and the fastest man in the NFL. He was the the fastest man in the NFL on that play. He he turned that corner and nobody was going to nobody was going to stop him. And then to have Butt get the six kicks and all go through the uprights, which was a great thing for him. And we're we're all pulling for him. He's he's done such a great job for us and for him to to have a nice day like this, I think was was a to him and it the hard work that he's put in. So, anyways, I I'm I'm sure I'm missing missing people here, but um it's it's always good to win the NFL. We got a short week. We'll be right back in the office uh tomorrow, players and coaches, and uh we've got a practice tomorrow to get ourselves ready to play Buffalo, a good Buffalo team um there on Thanksgiving. So, with that, time's yours. >> Andy, could you could you elaborate a little bit on the dimension that Emmit's providing? I mean, obviously there's only one ball to go around, but it seems like he's um you you been more things. >> Yeah, so well, you can catch and uh he can block, which is good. Those are things that uh you don't always know coming into when they become yours. Normally, if a guy's a good runner in college, he's probably going to be halfway decent for you in that game. But here he is catching the football the way he is. We're asking him to do a lot of different stuff in the past game, and then he's picked up on the blitzes uh and the different looks that people have given us, and when and when he had an opportunity with the pickups, he's done well there. So, and then the screen game, he's worked worked that into uh being patient enough to get out there and catch, get himself upfield in line with the the big guys. >> Has it Has it been a while or can you recall having one two punch with your backs that that these guys seem to provide right now with Kenneth and and >> Yeah, um I'll tell you no so you can write the story, but I mean I've I mean I've been fortunate to have good I've been fortunate to have good backs. I mean I've in my career as a coach. So, been lucky that way. We've normally had one or two of them that we felt comfortable with, but don't write that. Just get what you want there. Bye. >> Is it a classic trap game given what you have coming up starting Thursday? You've got a very young team. So, how were you able to >> Yeah. It's a good question. I mean that comes from the locker room. You have the the veteran players there, that senior leadership there. Those guys don't let anything slide. Um, they understand where we're at in the season and the importance of of it and that every game counts and they hammer that point home. Coaches do a nice job with it, but for for that peer hearing it from a peer is is um I think is is important and our guys they don't let anything slide there. >> Where do you see that you guys have improved the most over the last three weeks? >> Yeah, I think again, this is where the young guys come in. I just think if you look at the young guys and they're having opportunities to play and then stacking games and still getting better as they go. Um, it's small things but important things as we grow. And we knew that coming into training camp. You guys were all there and we knew there were going to be some hiccups along the way and it was important that you just kind of keep keep going. Coaches coach, players keep playing and learning. So I think the teaching by the coaches these guys being diligent with learning it and then retaining it so you don't make the same mistake twice becomes important. So we're we're seeing those little things and helping us become a better team. So >> What what's been the key to his emergence this year of being more of a force than he been? >> Yeah, he got married. His wife his wife's actually a better athlete than he is, which is want to sign his kids right now. Yeah. Um, now listen, he George is all business whether it's practice walkthrough game 100 miles an hour. He's smart tough, all those things. I mean, he just he's relentless. If you're going to play him, play against them, he's not the flashiest guy, but he's going to keep bringing it on you. And he's got he's developed some moves some skill there that that he's worked hard on. >> Yeah, so they played quite a little bit of shell coverage. Within that they they they'll bring five guys at times and so they're willing to give up a zone. And you got to you got to be able to find the spot and then there are normally small windows and you got to be able to shoot those spots. So we've got a couple of guys that know how to do that and and Pat knows how to shoot it, which is which is good, but >> Yeah, so when I'm done with you, I'm going back to the office. So it's a short drive. You're right there. Turn the page fast. >> All right, good. >> Yeah, I thought we got better and better each and every game, you know. That's what this this league's all about and we were able to come in and play good football and just consistently get better at people to the team and you can see the the offense getting better and better throughout and so definitely big wins for us and we'll try to keep that progression throughout the rest of the season. >> Yeah, just it comes with the process of a season, you know. I think for me just in general feeling more comfortable out there, you know. I'm coming off the injury and so being able to stand in that pocket, make those throws and then guys are proving it. I mean, Rashee made a couple of super tough catches. Josh did a great job making getting himself open. Cyrus a crazy catch on the sideline and Xavier making the plays there at the end and so I I think it's it's really speaks to the team and how guys have worked that we can kind of attack everywhere. >> Pat, can you speak to the dimension that MVS added? I mean, obviously he's his own player, but doing this in the spot he's been in, what's that done for you guys overall? >> I mean, it's been big. I mean obviously when you lose Kenneth you lose a ton of production. And so these last two games not having him out there someone had to step up and kind of do that and Emmit did a great job of that running the ball tough between the tackles, breaking tackles, and then catching the ball out the backfield as well. And so you see the talent but you never know with a young guy because he hasn't been in that position where he's the lead back for an entire game and he stepped up to it these last few weeks. And I think that's going to help out a ton as we we get K9 back. >> Does it get you thinking at all about how once Kenneth is back how you deploy Emmit too and if there's some some elements that this might open up for you guys that maybe you haven't been able to >> I think I think it excites you more than anything. It just cuz like we've talked about earlier everybody's making plays and so it's hard for defenses to account for that. And so obviously when Kenneth gets back he's Kenneth so he's going to get a lot of touches and he's going to make a lot of big plays happen. But we'll be able to utilize Emmit's skill set as well. And then knowing that the the defenses have to kind of prepare for both. It's not like when Kenneth goes out the game and Emmit comes in they can kind of relax. They got another guy that's going to bring that energy and that excitement and so I'm I'm I'm super excited to get to get both those guys going. >> I think I think this is the third time in like 22 years >> Yeah I mean we've obviously played good football these last few weeks and I mean even looking back to the Denver game we had a lot of good moments then as well. And so I think after that Seattle game guys took it upon themselves to get better and better. And we've done that. And obviously we've won some games here. But now it's how can we continue to get even more even more success and and do even more. And so I'm excited for the for the rest of the season. But it's all going to start this weekend on Thursday night. And so it was a good win today but we're going to keep it moving forward. >> Pat were you able to actually watch the game during game last night? >> So I watched the first half and then I watched like the last I would say 10 minutes cuz 80th minute but it ended up being like 30 minutes. But no it was it was really cool to see them win that championship man. and I mean I just knowing how hard they worked and some of those girls have been here since the beginning of when we got the team back to Kansas City and um just to see the excitement on their faces. Uh it's going to be amazing for the city and I'm excited for them to be able to celebrate with it. >> Is that correct that you got on the pregame pregame zoom with them? >> I did not get on a pregame. I talked to them after after on a FaceTime after the game. Yeah yeah not I did not talk to them pregame. No I let them kind of go out there and handle it themselves. I did like the narration narr- I narrated the uh the video but um I want them to I I've always been about like let them go out there and be them and they they they did a great job of that all year long. They went through the ups and the downs of a season um they and they got hot at the end of the season and they went out there and won a championship. >> Just last thing on it, what did you try to get across to him post game? >> I think it was just a bunch of excitement at that point. You know when you celebrate it's just a bunch of excitement and so um I wish I could have been there in person. Obviously couldn't be um but at the same time we were there and we were watching that late night snack with the Chiefs and everybody was hyped up to see the current bring a championship back home to Kansas City. >> Patrick, is the injury something that is just completely closed off and not even in the mind anymore or are you shut? >> Um I mean yeah in the sense of like when you go out there and play I'm not thinking about it. I still do all the same stuff throughout the week trying to prepare myself and and that stuff I'll probably do the rest of my life um just because it makes me feel mentally prepared to go out there and have success um but as far as um when I'm on the field it's not like I'm thinking about it and it's kind of been like that for a while now and I think what's what's been the biggest thing is the recovery after the game. I think that's been something that's been been nice to see is that like after the game I'm not super sore like I was at the beginning of the year. Um I'm getting back to to who I am and uh I'm excited for the the next few weeks here. >> Patrick Travis could have backed off the ankle stuff in this game maybe not played so on but he had a go and had the day that he did. What does that say about him? >> I mean that's that's Travis. I mean that you you can't take that dude off the football field. He loves it um and he goes out there and has success when he plays cuz he he he loves it that much. He competes. He's going to do whatever it takes to help the team win and um I mean he made a couple big plays for us there especially in the early part of the game and um that's the type of leader he is it and I've always say it it it makes my job as a quarterback easy. Like whenever you got a guy that that could take a game off or could take practice off or plays off, um because he's a Hall of Famer and he's the one that wants to get in there every single rep, um that kind of gives you the like the mindset to tell the other guys like hey like y'all want to take a rep off, look at this guy. And it it's just easy for me as a leader um to have someone like that on my team. >> A couple days now this is a season altering game. Not necessarily we can talk about it. How quickly do you switch gears and what's your process of just getting ready for Buffalo in a few days now? >> I'll make it to bedtime when I put the kids down and then I'll be studying the Buffalo Bills, so it'll be a pretty quick process. >> Last one. >> Patrick, for Maxima in Mexico tonight we have the Mexico City game. So would would you like to be back and play again in Mexico? >> I thought it was awesome playing at Azteca. I mean just the history there, the environment, the crowd it was rocking um and it it was really cool experience for me and so I'm always I'm always open to going back and playing there and I remember watching in the World Cup and watching the the national team from Mexico playing there and how crazy it was and how much passion the fans have. It kind of took me back to our time there and so I'll be watching that game tonight. It'll be a great football game um but it's always a great venue for the NFL. >> Thanks Patrick. >> What are you doing this week? >> I mean affecting the quarterback in any way possible to to help the team out, whether that's sacks, hits, hurries, pressures, batted balls, anything in between uh you know ultimately to help help the defense, help the team. You know so sacks are important but yeah. >> What does it say about the team that you guys are able to take care of these three games, get wins and now you move on to to be a tougher part of your schedule? >> Yeah I mean you take you take every every week in a time, one game at a time. You focus you know obviously one practice at a time, one game at a time, each opponent you know you focus all on them. Now we're on to Buffalo you know big challenge obviously ahead and you know we're going to dive right into those guys. >> What were just some of the keys today uh I was seeing new quarterback for Arizona what that can pose challenges as well as opportunity kind of? >> Yeah I mean similar similar to every week you know always starts with stopping the run game. You know, they had a good get run game going. So, trying to make them as one-dimensional as we can. And then uh you know, they have a great tight end. They got good receivers. So, uh making sure we handle those guys and uh make plays when the opportunity arises. So, I think we did a good job of that. Obviously, watching the tape, there's always going to be stuff to to correct and get better from, but I think we did a good job. It was a great team win. >> George, with a short week, I mean, how how quickly are you Yeah, you got to replace yourself, but how how quickly are you turning your attention Andy said he's driving right over the facility now. Um how do you how do you treat it? >> Yeah, I mean, I'll go I'll go home get get a little bit of treatment and probably watch this game, flush it out, and then right on to Buffalo by tonight. So, it's a short week. Everybody's going to be on point and uh we have a lot of respect for Buffalo. >> George, anticipate like where you going to be at that you're watching Buffalo stuff? >> Probably before before that even. Yeah. >> George, from a sack standpoint, you you picked your stride. I guess is there anything that you can point to that you know that has gotten you to this point where you're where you're you're able to accumulate a couple each week and take >> No, I mean, it just it just always just keep going. I mean, never get discouraged when you're not getting home. Uh you know, there's been there's been times where you go multiple games, months. I mean, my rookie year, I went all the way to Thanksgiving without getting a sack. So, always keep keep swinging. I'm always throwing my fastball, always trying to get to get after the quarterback, affect the quarterback really any way we can. And then, you know, when the defensive line's playing all together, front and back end with the DBs and linebackers, everybody's playing together, good things happen. So, uh it's really a team effort. You know, sacks, yeah, might be an individual statistic, but takes everybody to get them. You know, like the the one we had today, our Mason did a great job getting the wind of the quarterback. So, it's not just an individual stat in my opinion. >> Do you think Ashton's going to take another step >> Yeah, I mean, he you know, he was uh he was a little banged up in camp and all that kind of stuff, obviously, but he's a beast. I mean, I've known Ashton uh for a few years now just because we we shared staffs and I go out there Louisville and train in the off season and uh they uh they want me to talk with him and all this stuff and it uh it was crazy when he got drafted here obviously. Just, you know, I'm happy for his success. You know, I try to to help him out in every way I can. And uh yeah, I think he's just going to keep climbing climbing getting better cuz he's a heck of a football player. >> Couple more. >> Thank you guys. >> Yeah, honestly I just wanted to get downhill right away kind of set the tone for the offense and you know as a as a defender man setting the tone like that they don't want to they don't want to tackle the rest of the game after that so I'm kind of just you know just setting the tone for the offense. >> Yeah, very comfortable. I feel like just the guys trusting me up front Pat and all those guys having trust in me I think it just makes my job a lot easier to go out there and just you know be myself. >> Yeah, man. Just Pat being Pat man making plays getting the offense together and he's been making some great plays. We've been having some great drives and putting up a lot of points so I'm just really blessed to be playing with him. >> Yeah, I think just the adversity I've been through in my life kind of not taking anything for granted so whatever opportunity I get to help the team I'm just willing to go out there and make plays so I think just going through a lot of adversity man I think that's helped me kind of just prepare and be super super hungry to go out there and make plays for the team to win. >> Uh it's cool but I honestly just want to win a Super Bowl and win the next game focus on Buffalo all that stuff comes with it but just focus on helping the team win. >> It's going to be great. Quick turnaround so we got to go back and watch film and everything like that but it's going to be really exciting you know playing on Thanksgiving it's going to be a big big spotlight game and you know hopefully get some good to give them food and stuff too after. >> Yeah, he's done a lot, man. I think just how we practice, like how we push each other every single day, um we get the most out of each other and I think that's the biggest thing about me and Kenneth. We're both hungry guys. We go out there and work our butts off. We both want to help the team win and so just like him being there in practice really pushes me to be the best version of myself when I'm out there on the field. >> This is a quick turnaround in Buffalo. How's that process going to go for you? >> Um yeah, just go watch film today, uh recover my body as much as possible, we get back in the building tomorrow and just get ready to work. >> Thank you, Thank you. >> God bless. Yep. >> All right, see you.

Uh, and that's the luxury of being a quarterback. But, uh, I think, uh, Coach Benemy does a great job of making sure that everybody keeps that level head and, uh, just does their job and, uh, never, you know, second guesses when they're supposed to be when their numbers called or, uh, you know, never let the ball surprise you when you're not the the primary in in every single route. So, it's a right now it's uh, we're all growing and and we're catching stride and it was good to see everybody out there playing well together. >> I try to tell everybody, watch tape, cuz when I watch tape, I see you wham blocking. How do you handle these hours ahead? >> You just got to love football, man. You know, I You can roll the ball. You can roll the ball out in the Walmart parking lot on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. It doesn't matter which day it is. I you're going to see me show up because I love this game. And um you know the the short weeks are you know they can be a little bit of a battle for the for the body. But on top of that um when it's game day and the balls snap your love for the game better show up and your love for your teammates better show up. So >> I don't get to meet Taylor. I don't get to ride in his car. This is as close as I get. But this is awesome, man. I I do want to value every second with you. >> Come on. I'm right here with you, baby. The voice counts. >> All right. Yeah, I thought we got better and better each and every game, you know. Um that's what this this league is all about. And um we were able to come in and play good football and just consistently get better, add um people to the team and um you can see the the offense getting better and better throughout. And so um definitely big wins for us. Um and we'll try to keep that progression throughout the rest of the season. >> Seems like a heavy trust right now in all the pass captures across the board. You know, I think for me just in general feel more comfortable out there. you know, I'm uh coming off the injury and so being able to stand in that pocket, make those throws and then guys are proving it. I mean, Rashid made a couple super tough catches. Um Josh did a great job making getting himself open, Cyrus, a crazy catch on the sideline and Xavier making the plays there at the end. And so, um I think it's it's really speaks to the team and how guys have worked that we can kind of attack everywhere. >> Can you speak to the dimension that Emtts added? I mean, obviously he's his own player, but [snorts] doing this in the spot he's been in, what's that done for you guys overall? I mean, it's been big. I mean, obviously when you lose Kenneth, you lose a ton of production. Um, and so these last two games, not having him out there, someone had to step up and kind of do that. And EMTT did a great job of that, running the ball tough between the tackles, breaking tackles, um, and then catching the ball on the back foot as well. And so, um, you see the talent, but you never know with the young guy cuz he hasn't been that position where he's the lead back um, for an entire game and he stepped up to it these last few weeks. Um, and I think that's going to help out a ton as we we get K9 back. Does it get you thinking at all about how you know once Kenneth's back, you know, how you deploy EMTT too and that there's some some elements that this might open up for you guys that maybe you haven't been able to >> I think I think it excites you more than anything. Um just cuz like we've talked about earlier, everybody's making plays and so it's hard for defenses to account for that. Um and so um obviously when Kenneth gets back, he's Kenneth so he's going to get a lot of touches and he's going to make a lot of big plays happen. Um but we'll be able to utilize Emit's skill set as well. Um, and then knowing that the defenses have to kind of prepare for both. It's not like when Kenneth goes out the game and Emtt comes in, they can kind of relax. They got another guy that's going to bring that energy and that excitement. And so, um, I'm I'm I'm super excited to get to get both those guys going. >> Patrick, I think this is the third time in like 22 years that you scored 34 points in three consecutive games. >> You got injuries up front, tennis. What does that say about where the offense is now and where? Yeah, I mean we've obviously u played good football these last few weeks and I mean even looking back to the Denver game, we had a lot of good moments then as well. And so um I think after that Seattle game, guys took it upon themselves to get better and better. Um and we've done that. Um and obviously we've won some games here. Um but now it's how can we continue to get even more even more success and and do even more and so uh I'm excited for the for the rest of the season. Um but it's all going to start this weekend on Thursday night and so uh it was a good win today but we're going to keep it moving forward. Patrick, were you able to actually watch the game, current game last night? >> I So, I watched the first half and then I watched like the last um I would say 10 minutes cuz it was 80th minute, but it ended up being like 30 minutes. Um but no, it was it was really cool um to see them win that championship, man. I mean, I just knowing how hard they worked and some of those girls have been here since the beginning of when we got the team back to Kansas City and um just to see the excitement on their faces. Uh it's going to be amazing for the city and I'm excited for them to be able to celebrate with it. Is that correct that you got on the pregame a pregame zoom with them? >> I did not get on a pregame. I talked to him after after on a FaceTime after the game. Yeah. Yeah. Not I did not talk to him pregame, you know. I let them kind of go out there and handle it themselves. I did like the nar I narrated the uh the video, but um I want them to I've always been about like let them go out there and be them. And they they they did a great job with that all year long. They went through the ups and downs of a season. Um they and they got hot at the end of the season and they went out there and won a championship. Just last thing on it, what did you try to get across to him post game? >> I think it was just a bunch of excitement at that point. You know, when you celebrate, it's just a bunch of excitement and so um I wish I could have been there in person. Obviously couldn't be. Um but at the same time, we were there and we were watching that late night snack with the Chiefs and everybody was hyped up to see the current bring a championship back home to Kansas City. >> And Patrick, is the injury something that is just completely closed off and not even in the mind anymore? Um, I mean, yeah, in a sense of like when you go out there and play, I'm not thinking about it. I still do all the same stuff throughout the week, trying to prepare myself and and that stuff I'll probably do the rest of my life. Um, just because it makes me feel mentally prepared to go out there and have success. Um, but as far as um, when I'm on the field, it's not like I'm thinking about it. And it's kind of been like that for a while now. And I think what's what's been the biggest thing is the recovery after the game. I think that's been something that's been been nice to see is that like after the game, I'm not super sore like I was at the beginning of the year. Um, I'm getting back to to who I am and I'm excited for the the next few weeks here. >> Patrick Travis could have backed off the ankle stuff in this game, maybe not played and so on, but he goes and has that he did. What does that say about? >> I mean, that's that's Travis. I mean, that you you can't take that dude off the football field. He loves it. Um, and he goes out there and has success when he plays cuz he he loves it that much. He competes. He's going to do whatever it takes to help the team win. And, um, I mean, he made a couple big plays for us there, especially in the early part of the game. And, um, that's the type of leader he is. it. And I've always say it it makes my job as a quarterback easy. Like whenever you got a guy that that could take a game off or could take practice off or plays off um because he's a Hall of Famer and he's the one that wants to get in there every single rep. Um that kind of gives you the like the mindset to tell the other guys like, "Hey, like y'all want to take a rep off. Look at this guy." And it it's just easy for me as a leader um to have someone like that on my team. And >> couple days now, this is a seasonal alter game. They're not here. We can talk about it. How quickly do you switch gears and what's your process of just getting ready for Buffalo? I'll make it to bedtime when I put the kids down and then I'll be studying the Buffalo Bills. So, it'll be a pretty quick process. >> Last one. >> Patrick, for Maxim in Mexico, tonight we have the Mexico City game. So, would you like to be back and play against Mexico? >> I thought it was awesome playing Aztec. I mean, just the history there, the environment, the crowd, it was rocking. Um, and uh it it was really cool experience for me. And so, I'm always I'm always open to going back and playing there. Uh it kind of took me back to our time there and so I'll be watching that game tonight. It'll be a great football game. Um but uh it's always a great venue for the NFL. >> Thanks. >> For all of you high school or collegiate wrestlers out there. You loved Noah Williams today. How about the two-point takedown? Did you wrestle in high school? >> I did not wrestle in high school, but you know, I got great coaches here that you know got spags for tackling. You know, they're all about tackling here. So, but no, I did not do wrestling in high school. So, >> what about that play where you like pick him up and throw him down? >> Yeah, I was I was kind of surprised. He just ended up on my shoulders and, you know, I tried to like his weight was going back and I had to kind of stable him. Everybody's >> He's number 20 in your program, No Williams, and he's quickly emerging as one of the top corners in this league. So I'm like the only place he can go is outside. So I was getting off the block, you know, I was trying to shed him. Could have got off better, but I knew the marker was right there and I just, you know, big collision and um I knew it was a stop. Yes, sir. >> But honestly, people want to make the kill shot, but you making the form tackle is something that you do now with regularity. Um, you know, it's getting, you know, later into the season where we don't have pads on during practice. And, um, now I got to emphasize my form, you know, en envision it even if we're not, you know, thud, you know, thud tackle or tackling the bag, but any chance I get, you know, I put myself in that situation. They try to go boundary on you and go deep, but you made a terrific play there. What about that play and making those kind of plays down the field? >> Yeah. Um, you know, on our defense, we echo deny the deep shots cuz obviously nobody likes explosives on their defense and um yeah, you know, I could I could always play it better on both of them. And um but luckily, you know, at the end of the day, they didn't catch the ball and you know, that that's a win for the KC defense. >> How much of this defense though is working? You're getting pressure up front. You're getting coverage on the back end. >> Yeah, everybody's clicking throughout, you know, the last three weeks. Um we've been firing all cylinders and um this is good momentum we need to take into going into Buffalo Thanksgiving. >> Speaking of that, one final question. How do you deal It's not days, it's hours. It's really ours. It's Wednesday of Buffalo week right now. >> Yeah. Yeah. I mean, enjoy this win for a couple hours and then I'm on to the film. We know who we got. Josh Allen. Thanksgiving prime time. You know, everybody's going to be watching it. So, I'm excited and um looking forward to it. Got to got to got to um flip the script. There go my son Jane, the one and only. >> Number 20, Noah Williams. Heck of a game, heck of a season. >> Yeah, appreciate you trying to set the tone. >> Yeah, honestly, I just wanted to get downhill right away. um kind of set the tone for the offense and you know as a as a defender man setting the tone like that they don't want to they don't want to tackle the rest of the game after that. So um kind of just you know just setting the tone for the offense. >> And how much more comfortable do you feel after having two starts like this under your belt this way and the sense of being more of a factor? >> Yeah, very comfortable. I feel like just the guys trusting me up front. Um Pat and all those guys having trusted me. I think it just makes my job a lot easier to go out there and just, you know, be myself. And then what have you been seeing from Pat here the last couple weeks? >> Yeah, man. Just Pat being Pat, man, making plays. Um, getting the offense together and he's been making some great plays. We've been having some great drives and putting up a lot of points. So, I'm just really blessed to be playing with him. >> You think it is from your past experiences college and otherwise you really? >> Yeah, I think just the adversity I've been through in my life. Um, kind of not taking anything for granted. So, whatever opportunity I get to help the team, uh, I'm just willing to go out there and, uh, make plays. So, I think just, uh, going through a lot of adversity, man, I think that's helped me kind of just prepare and be super super hungry to go out there and make plays for the team to win. What's that like for you? >> Uh, it's cool, but I honestly just want to win a Super Bowl and win the next game. Focus on Buffalo. All that stuff um comes with it, but just focus on helping the team win. What is it like feeling like you're going to face Buffalo, big rival, short week, Thanksgiving, what's >> going to be great. Um, a quick turnaround, so we got to go back and watch film and everything like that. But it's going to be really exciting, you know, playing on Thanksgiving. It's going to be a big big spotlight game and, you know, hopefully get some good Thanksgiving food and stuff too after. >> Got a lot of guys to learn from here, but specifically how much have you sort of learned from Kenneth in particular? What what has he done to help you? >> Yeah, he's done a lot, man. And I think just how we practice, like how we push each other every single day, um we get the most out of each other. And I think that's the biggest thing about me and Kenneth. We're both hungry guys. We go out there and work our butts off. We both want to help the team win. And so just like him being there in practice really pushes me to be the best version of myself when I'm out there on the field. >> This is a quick turn around. How's that process going to go for you? >> Um yeah, just go watch film today. Uh recover my body as much as possible. We get back in the building tomorrow and just get ready to work. >> Thank you everybody. Thank you. >> God bless. Yeah. >> All right. The Chiefs win it 34-7 over the Arizona Cardinals. Fun game again. Patrick Mahomes. Uh over two touchdown passes, no interceptions. It hadn't happened since 2021. It's his best quarterback rating in seven seasons. And today it'll only go up from here. >> Yeah, he's just playing some incredible football right now. And I think it says so much about our team that after that frankly devastating loss in Denver where we have the game right, we end up not winning it. we find a way to win these three games in a row really in dominant fashion scoring at least 34 points in each and every one of them to set ourselves up for the run that we're going to face here moving forward but says a lot about the character of our team a lot of teams would let their season fall apart after that game in Denver we didn't >> and that game that's going to be a 30 plus game >> and a win >> y >> with the call at the end okay there were some other milestones here in this as but the the you're thinking we could sit here and spew out stats but the offense is able to attack with the run and the pass, able to attack the width of the field and vertical as well. text: This is "Between the Lines," presented by Gatorade .  I'm Taden Everett.  This is Ben Lieber.  The Vikings lose 35:10 in Mexico City to the San Francisco 49ers. They now have seven wins and three losses on the season, Ben. And, as we saw against the Packers, it was a very team-oriented style of play that didn't seem to translate into this match. In the first quarter, it seemed like you were building something.  Where do you think it all went wrong? Well, for us in defense, that was the main intrigue of the match.  Defensively, it seemed like the Niners had the answers for everything.  They were n't nervous at all.  We couldn't get them out of their rhythm.  They didn't attack through the carry as I expected, but it was enough to set up a fake pass game. I was very impressed with how they built routes, found free zones, and chose timing.  And Brock Purdy was simply unmoved.  We've seen it on video, but it's incredible to see it with our own eyes. True.  The timing was interesting, as they managed to get Jordan Love to throw fast last week.  But this week was different, as Purdy was able to complete many of those passes.  What did he do so effectively that really made the Vikings defense surrender? Well, it's actually Shanahan and his concepts. They did a great job of narrowing the distance between their receivers, meaning they played closer to center. They were close to the Tekli.  So they were in a tight formation, which allowed them to get to the center of the field faster. And they were great at stacking their receivers, creating pairs or trios of players.  For us, as defenders, it's very difficult to get to the second or third player if they're standing in a bunch.  You can hit the first one, knock him out of his rhythm, but there is always a player behind him who gets free space. I think they did it quite often: if we didn't get to the quarterback, that second or third player would be completely free, and we just couldn't block him.   Were you able to communicate with...Was it just one player or multiple? I spoke with Aaron Jones and Joshua Metellus. Can you describe the general mood that prevailed there?  How was it? You know, surprisingly positive.  Um, Joshua Metellus, I think, said it best: "Sometimes you have to get slapped in the face to understand where your team is at." And not just in terms of character, but also in terms of strategy and execution, if we put the 49ers at the level of top teams, where do we stand? And it is obvious that we are much lower. So I think it was a good wake-up call for the boys, and that's how they feel in the locker room: the season is still long, there are a lot of matches ahead, and we certainly haven't reached our peak yet. So they will come back, analyze this "slap" and, hopefully, draw the right conclusions. This was only Kirk Cousins' second game since returning to the purple and gold uniform, and you could see how difficult it was for the offense to move down the field.  What impressed you most about the attacking game? Well, everything was quite difficult.  You know, most of the plays were only for 5-6 yards.  If we wanted to score, it had to be long, sustained drives, and we just lacked explosive power.  And the only explosive moment with Justin Jefferson in midfield, when he tried to beat a defender, ended in a turnover.  So even when we have an explosive moment, we can't execute it and lose the ball again .  Aaron Jones said their defensive line did a great job, constantly changing tactics.  They set up this defense with two deep safeties.  They built the game to only give away what the defense allowed, so the game was just that, and we made too many mistakes. Well, let's move on, leaving everything behind.  On Sunday, the game against the Falcons is at US Bank Stadium.  We're coming home , and it's wonderful.  Finally back at US Bank Stadium after three out of the last four away games.  What lessons can you take from this match to use as you prepare for Sunday's game against the Falcons? You know, I think defensively we might have to be a little more creative when we see these tight formations, stacks, and clusters of players—we need to have an answer for that.  And it's not that every team can play like the Niners.  The Niners, I mean, played as cohesively as any other team, and I don't think anyone can just take that plan and say, " Hey, we're going to do exactly the same thing."  We have to do a better job of confusing quarterbacks on defense. Today we didn't do it in the best way.  And I think that in attack we did a good job of protecting the pass, but I think we could have played better.  And I know that Darriso's injury and his constant absences from the lineup were not good.  We need to play more effectively on the ball.  So there's still a lot of work ahead of the offense . Well, one thing is for sure: NFL fans in Mexico City don't have to work for anything.  They bring real energy.  The stadium was as loud as possible all this time.  What were your feelings on the field? That was incredible, Tatum.  I don't know about you, but I assume you felt the same way .  When the game started, all I could say was "wow."  It was just an amazing atmosphere.  Not only did this match feel like a playoff game, It's true, yes. this energy—we feel the same when we go to Europe.  You know, the fans, I think they're so passionate because they don't see that often.  And they cheered throughout the entire game, all 60 minutes.  And I can't believe they stayed, even when the outcome was decided and we and they were replacing key players.  The stadium was still about 75% full. They must have enjoyed every last moment.  Well, it's time for us to get on the plane to Minnesota, it was "Between the Lines" presented by Gatorade, and we'll see you on Sunday for the game against the Falcons.
