title: The big picture on Heather Dinich's projected CFP bracket 🏈🏆 | Get Up YouTube Exclusive
text: Welcome into this Get Up exclusive on YouTube. I'm Greeny. That's Heather and Paul who are with me after another chaotic weekend in college football and in advance of this week's CFP rankings. So, let's take a look at what Heather thinks they will be or at least thinks they should be. These are Heather's updated brackets after the weekend that was Georgia is one, Utah is two, Texas jumping up to three, Alabama four, Notre Dame at five, Miami, UCLA after that tough loss, Tennessee, Wake Forest, BYU, Indiana falling to 12. Remember, Boise State is the highest ranked team in the group of six, which means at this moment they would get in. Heather, take us through some of the big picture thinking on these rankings. Greeny, with UCLA dropping out, I think this is finally the week that the committee compares its top two loss teams side by side, which are Alabama and Texas. And you have heard me say for weeks, I think Texas finally has a case to be the committee's top two loss team because of its resume. Well, with UCLA no longer as a buffer between those two teams and with Alabama playing an FCS team, Texas beating up on Arkansas, yes, but the committee was looking for consistency out of the Longhorns, they got it. I think Texas jumps Alabama as the top two loss team. And then at the bottom, listen, you Indiana is in trouble any way you slice it, but I don't think they fall all the way to that number 12 spot. I could be wrong. This is my biggest question. I had them at 11. And here's why. They beat USC. They have a better strength of schedule than Texas Tech. The win against USC is still better than Texas Tech's wins against Arizona and Houston. And with Nebraska beating Ohio State, people need to remember that Indiana beat Nebraska on the road, something the Buckeyes couldn't do. So, when you take all of that into consideration, and I know the committee will again continue to question that Indiana offense as they use both quarterbacks, Josh Hoover and Grant Wilson again, but that's how it shook out. >> All right, so I'll get to all the Big 10 stuff in a second, but Paul, let's start at the very top there as Heather was laying it out with Texas and Alabama. Georgia, I don't think anyone questions them being at the top as they are. How about the Texas Alabama of it all, Paul? >> Yeah, my biggest issue isn't Texas over Alabama. It's Alabama over Tennessee. And I know I sound like one of those guys in the upper deck at Neland Stadium screaming at Heather Dennis right now daring to wear orange. But Greenie, uh I as we get toward the end of the season, I can't get over the fact that Tennessee not only beat Alabama at Neland Stadium. They beat them badly. Uh, I know Tennessee threw it away the next week against South Carolina, but Alabama's losses continue, excuse me, Alabama's wins continue to be devalued with every single week. And I know it's a close call, but I think head-to-head should really matter. That's my biggest quibble. Indiana, I think, is in more trouble than Heather thinks they are. Um, I and and I I try to take out the signetti factor. he should not factor into it. Although he is fairly annoying with his criticism and trolling of the media, he picked a bad week to do that. >> Let's hold off that that thought a minute. I let me go back to the Tennessee of it all, Heather, because that that this was a big deal all year last year with the head-to-head between Miami and Notre Dame, right? And the committee took it all the way to the last week and then flipped it. And my understanding, and I'm I'm setting you up to talk about this cuz I just don't assume that everyone watching this knows the way they do it, is they put these teams in pods, and if they're in different pods, meaning they basically think that they're not on the same level, then the head-to-head doesn't come into play. If they had them in the same level, then the head-to-head would come into play. And so what the committee is telling us, not what Heather is telling us, what the committee is telling us is they don't consider Tennessee and Alabama to be on the same level. Am I getting that right? You nailed it. And it's because there are too many teams between them to consider them comparable, which is one of the reasons UCLA where they drop is important because I have UCLA still ahead of Tennessee. That might not happen. Another one of my questions is UCLA behind the balls or ahead of them after losing to Michigan? Because I still think the committee will have Miami and Notre Dame and UCLA in between um Alabama and Tennessee. And when you talk about those pods or groups, there are four teams of groupings that they're voting on. And they can compare as many as four teams side by side on their screens. But remember, the tricky part about the selection committee's criteria and metrics, guys, is that they are not weighted. They are subjective, right? So, even if they were right next to each other, you could still have someone in that room who says, "I think Alabama's better than Tennessee on the field." Period. I'm going to keep them ranked that way. Even if they're right next to each other, it's not weighted. It is a tiebreaker if they want to refer to it. So, that's why it's kind of tricky. And that's what has always frustrated me. And this really is a conversation that we've had going back to college basketball much more than football. There are some sports that have to be judged subjectively, Paul, right? Like I mean, figure skating and gymnastics and someone has to judge these things because people aren't competing against each other, but most what what most of us love about sports is that these games are decided on fields or courts or rinks or wherever they are played. And if the two of them played each other as these two teams did, it would make me insane that a person would say, well, it remains my opinion that this other team is better. You know, that that strikes me as the degree of of um uh I don't know, arrogance that is required in saying in my opinion, this team is better than this one even though they played each other and the result the result worked the other way. That I think is what frustrates a lot of people. Well, part of the problem, Greenie, is that that this committee sends out a person every Tuesday night. It doesn't matter who it is. Uh, and they never communicate correctly. Uh, it's just that we get lost in the weeds. And you sat every Sunday and Monday, Tuesday, every every day of the week, you sit next to former athletes, uh, as I do on the weekends. And former athletes put a lot of premium on one thing, head-to-head. And that's why the the America has such a difficult time and I say this with the mo the most respect in the world toward Heather. When she tries to explain the mindset of the committee, they tear their hair out and they want to throw things at Heather because all she's doing is representing what they're thinking, but they don't like the way this committee thinks. >> That's exactly right. For I mean, let the record show and I don't even think this needs to be addressed, but I'm glad to address it. Heather is the messenger. You're yelling at the messenger for crying out loud. She's telling you what these people are doing because it's her job to cover what they're doing. The ones you're mad at are the rest of them. Uh that as Trevor Mannis used to say, who are sitting in that room eating shrimp and croissants and and you're yelling at them and Okay, let's go to the Big 10. Um Heather, for the first time in 5 years, the AP rankings came out over the weekend and of course we live in the CFP rankings, but the AP rankings are interesting if nothing else. It's the first time in five years there's no Big 10 team in the top five as you see there on the screen since November of 2021. How would you describe where things stand for the Big 10 right now? >> Well, the Big 10 is in big trouble only if you thought they were going to have four or five teams in the College Football Playoff coming into this season. The reality is they're still probably going to have two. That's not great. If you're Big 10 commissioner Tony Patiti, you want to have four or five. But here's the reality. USC is probably going to beat UCLA and knock them out of the college football playoff, but you have Oregon and Iowa who are sitting there on the bubble and can move in. So you can still have Oregon or Iowa getting in with Indiana if Indiana's not in the college football playoff and they're sitting there. Again, that's why where the Hooers are on Tuesday night is so important because if they are not in that 12 spot, if they're at 11 or 10 and they are not in the Big 10 Championship game, they don't have to risk losing another game. They're just sitting there. Sort of like BYU, right? And that's another team to watch on Tuesday night. So, if you have the the Big 10 champ is guaranteed to be in. And then that second team, is it Indiana? We'll see on Tuesday night. >> What do you think of of the big picture look at the Big 10 right now, Paul? >> Well, I happen to be uh in Alabama this morning, Greeney, home of the SEC headquarters, and you can hear the laughter coming out of that building right now. Uh because the Big 10 just showed up at media days in July bragging about owning the world and it it has come back to haunt them. Uh I I think Oregon is amazingly the best team in the Big 10 right now. And and I say that because I think I told you about six weeks ago that they were dead in the biggest disappointment. Remember they started the season number two, but they have survived. Uh I think Indiana is in the biggest trouble. That that that loss was shattering over the weekend. UCLA losing really shouldn't have surprised anybody. Um and and Heather's right. I can't imagine them winning with somebody from the stands at quarterback uh on Saturday uh against USC, but but that's where we are. Uh and and you know, I mentioned Signetti earlier. I mean, he he just started mouththing off at the wrong time. And I don't know many people who feel sorry for Curt Signetti this morning. >> I also can't remember a time, Heather, when the Ohio State Michigan game felt like it feels this weekend. that at least one or the other has been extraordinarily relevant every year for what feels like forever and in many cases both. This year we're in a situation where it's neither. What's next for these two? >> Well, both of these teams need to make some staff changes and I do not see it coming at the head coach position. I mean, here's the reality with both of these programs. You can spend millions of dollars on the transfer portal and you can misfire and not have a great season if you don't have the right guys on staff. You don't have the depth that you need. And how many people have a national championship winning backup quarterback on their ro roster ready to hop into the lineup? This is all a result of NIL and the portal. And it's the same thing can be said for Lane Kein, right? You got injuries at key places. You don't have the depth to deal with it. You misfire in the portal on Sam Levit. I mean, these Ohio State and Michigan are a microcosm right now of the bigger picture of college football. All the money in the world does not guarantee you a spot right now in the college football playoff. >> Paul, final word. Uh, I what what's so extraordinary to me is is I I go to the Iron Bowl every year and then I'm told by people at Michigan, Ohio State is so much bigger. But Greeny, the Iron Bowl is Saturday, Michigan State and College Game Day, which is a personification of the sport will be at Duke Wake Forest. What else do you need to know about college football than that? >> It's a weird time, but it is probably the beginning of a new time for a variety of different reasons. And that is all the time we have for today's Get Up exclusive on YouTube. Remember, we're with you every weekday morning starting at 8 a.m. Eastern on ESPN.
